motionBlur.title: How to add motion blur to video on iPhone for free
motionBlur.description: Watch a ByteWave motion blur comparison, then apply the effect on iPhone and choose its strength.
motionBlur.intro: Open Advanced → Motion Blur in ByteWave, choose a strength and tap Apply. Watch the harbor comparison and try the steps on your clip.
motionBlur.aria: Motion blur comparison: original harbor on the left, ByteWave motion blur on the right
motionBlur.caption: The same harbor scene plays in both halves for 19.5 seconds, with original on the left and motion blur on the right. No audio.
motionBlur.observe: Watch the moving boat edges, masts and shore. Blur softens details along motion. Play and pause to compare individual frames.
motionBlur.step1: Open your video. Add a clip with Add Media if needed, then select its thumbnail.
motionBlur.step2: Open the editing tools. Tap the hexagonal button beside the preview and choose Advanced.
motionBlur.step3: Choose Motion Blur. Select the pink Motion Blur tile in Advanced.
motionBlur.step4: Set the strength and apply. Move the slider from 1 to 100 and tap Apply.
motionBlur.step5: Wait for processing, then play the clip to check the effect across its movement.
motionBlur.exportNote: To save the result, open the tools menu and choose Export.
motionBlur.strength1: Start with a low value to preserve detail. Increase it and review at the speed you plan to export.
motionBlur.strength2: Camera movement can soften much of the frame. If it looks overly smeared, use a lower value on a new copy of the original clip.
motionBlur.differenceTitle: Motion blur and slow motion do different jobs
motionBlur.differenceText: Motion blur softens movement inside each picture; slow motion changes playback speed. For speed changes, read our
motionBlur.freeTitle: Free editing without a required account
motionBlur.privacyText: Motion blur is free in ByteWave, without an export watermark or required account. The local editor does not upload footage to ByteWave servers; optional online publishing follows separate rules in the
motionBlur.cta: Try it with your own footage. Apply motion blur and compare the result before exporting.

frameRate.title: Frame rate conversion for slow-motion video on iPhone
frameRate.description: Watch ordinary 0.1× slow motion beside ByteWave frame rate conversion and learn to use FRC.
frameRate.intro: Frame rate conversion (FRC) adds intermediate frames to smooth slow motion. Find it under Speed in ByteWave.
frameRate.aria: Hummingbird at 0.1×: regular slowdown left, ByteWave frame rate conversion right
frameRate.caption: The same three-second hummingbird recording slowed to 0.1× in both halves; ordinary slowdown left, ByteWave FRC right. No audio.
frameRate.stepsTitle: How to use frame rate conversion
frameRate.step1: Select your clip and choose Speed from the main editing menu.
frameRate.step2: Choose playback speed; enable FRC for smoother slow motion and Reverse for backward playback. This example uses 0.1× speed and 8× FRC.
frameRate.step3: Process and preview the movement before exporting.
frameRate.warp: If fast-moving edges warp or smear, try a less extreme slowdown.

frameRate.cta: Make your own slow-motion video in ByteWave.

temporalNoise.title: Temporal noise reduction for video on iPhone
temporalNoise.description: Compare original Apple example footage with ByteWave temporal noise reduction, including grain and moving edges.
temporalNoise.intro: Temporal noise reduction combines information from nearby frames to reduce video grain. Find Advanced → Temporal Noise Reduction in ByteWave's clip tools.
temporalNoise.comparisonTitle: Temporal noise reduction before and after
temporalNoise.aria: Apple foliage comparison: original on the left, ByteWave noise reduction on the right
temporalNoise.caption: Apple example footage, original on the left and ByteWave noise reduction on the right, playing together at normal speed without audio.
temporalNoise.step1: Select the clip and open its editing tools.
temporalNoise.step2: Open Advanced → Temporal Noise Reduction and apply the effect.
temporalNoise.step3: Preview the result, then export once you are satisfied.
temporalNoise.lookFor: Compare grain in dark areas; check that leaves and branches retain detail and moving edges have no trails. Full-screen playback helps see small differences.
temporalNoise.frcLink: slow motion with frame rate conversion
temporalNoise.cta: Try temporal noise reduction on your own footage.
